assertions.name: commutative_R_n_nakayama_id_diverges_from_grho
assertions.source: R_n commutative => nu=id => +1 on all V_lambda; but g_rho=q^{2 n(lambda)} gives -1 on the odd-n(lambda) partitions (exists for every n>=3) => nu != g_rho. INV-1 refutes the coinvariant route.

assertions.name: semisimple_nakayama_id_not_grho
assertions.source: semisimple => nu=id => +1 on every V_lambda; g_rho=q^{2 n(lambda)} != 1 for n(lambda)>0 (e.g. [2,1],[1^3]) => nu != g_rho. INV-2 refutes the CS_n / H_n(q) route.

assertions.name: nilcoxeter_local_single_simple

assertions.name: content_grading_differs_from_row_grading
assertions.source: the CONTENT grading n(lambda')-n(lambda) (Markov-trace pivotal twist, pruned #3529) gives a DIFFERENT zeta_4 sign than the ROW grading n(lambda) for some lambda => the one natural pivotal 'Nakayama-like' twist is the wrong (content) grading, not g_rho

assertions.name: grho_is_genuine_z2_grading_not_identity
assertions.source: both bar-even and bar-odd V_lambda exist at every n>=3 => g_rho is a nontrivial ZZ/2 grading at zeta_4 => categorically != a Nakayama automorphism (=id on symmetric H_n(q)/CS_n)

description: Formalize-first test of Delta_lambda open problem (i): is g_rho the Nakayama automorphism of a natural graded Frobenius structure? NO -- refuted. Symmetric algebras carrying V_lambda (coinvariant R_n commutative; CS_n/H_n(q) semisimple) have Nakayama=id (proved invariants) => +1, never the ROW grading q^{2 n(lambda)}; non-symmetric candidates (0-Hecke, nilCoxeter, gr H_n(q)) index simples by the wrong set; the one natural pivotal twist is the CONTENT grading (+1 at zeta_4, already pruned). g_rho is a pivotal/central ROW grading, not a Nakayama automorphism. No fit; nothing wired.

proved_invariants.INV-2: semisimple => every Frobenius form = sum c_lambda chi_lambda symmetric => nu=id

candidates_swept.markov_trace_pivotal_twist: CONTENT grading q^{2(n(lambda')-n(lambda))}, +1 at zeta_4, already pruned #3529 -- wrong (content, not row) grading

data.verdict: NO -- Angle A (g_rho = Nakayama automorphism of a natural graded Frobenius structure) is REFUTED, honestly and decisively. (1) On EVERY algebra whose simples are indexed by partitions lambda -- the coinvariant algebra R_n (COMMUTATIVE, INV-1) and the semisimple CS_n / generic H_n(q) (INV-2: every Frobenius form is a combination of symmetric characters) -- the Nakayama automorphism is the IDENTITY, acting as +1 (=q^0) on every V_lambda, NEVER the nontrivial ROW-grading scalar q^{2 n(lambda)} (= -1 on the odd-n(lambda) partitions). PROVED INVARIANTS [scope-(b)], not numeric near-misses. (2) The natural NON-symmetric graded Frobenius candidates with nontrivial Nakayama -- 0-Hecke H_n(0) (2^{n-1} composition simples), nilCoxeter NC_n (local, one simple), and the length-associated-graded gr H_n(q) (0-Hecke-type) -- index their simples by the WRONG set (p(n) != 2^{n-1} != 1), so structurally cannot carry a partition-indexed q^{2 n(lambda)} [scope-(a)]. (3) The ONE natural pivotal / ribbon 'Nakayama-like' twist theta_lambda = q^{2(n(lambda')-n(lambda))} is graded by the CONTENT sum (col-row), is +1 at zeta_4, and was ALREADY pruned (#3529/#3523) -- it is the CONTENT grading, NOT the ROW grading g_rho. CONSEQUENCE for open problem (i): the Nakayama route does NOT provide a self-contained categorical morphism for g_rho; the correct, already-derived home remains the GS/jet-order (fake-degree valuation) pivotal ROW grading. This negative SAVES the nakayama_eq_principalGrading Lean effort and refines the search. No fit; nothing wired.
data.answer: NO -- Nakayama automorphism of a natural graded Frobenius structure is NOT g_rho (the row grading q^{2 rho}); Angle A refuted
data.scope: (a)+(b) NEGATIVE -- symmetric cases by proved invariant (b), non-symmetric cases by wrong-index structural (a)
data.still_open: open problem (i) -- a self-contained categorical morphism for g_rho -- remains open; the pivotal/jet-order (fake-degree) ROW-grading route is the correct home; the Nakayama route is closed
